key_insight: Thresholding extreme vorticity and reconstructing velocity via Biot–Savart cleanly separates intermittency-driven effects from the broader turbulent cascade, showing which scaling features survive and which are altered by intermittent structures.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical filtering tool for diagnosing and modeling turbulent flows, helping engineers distinguish robust inertial-range behavior from intermittency that skews spectra, structure functions, and multifractal metrics.
method: Threshold vorticity to remove extreme intermittent regions.
Invert the Biot–Savart law to reconstruct filtered velocity fields.
Compare spectra, structure functions, multifractal spectra, and vortex-stretching/strain statistics before and after filtering.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that filtering preserves the energy-spectrum scaling while flattening the bottleneck and driving structure-function exponents toward Kolmogorov values, with the strongest changes seen in transverse exponents and multifractal range.
watch_item: Because the method removes extreme events by thresholding, the conclusions depend on the chosen cutoff and may alter physically important small-scale structures if applied too aggressively.
paper_title: Disentangling intermittent flow structure contributions to anomalous scaling and multifractality in turbulence
